title: Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage: Underpaid, Overstudied, and Still the Villain — Brought to You by People Who Have Never Adjudicated a Claim
description: A 2026 study in Health Affairs Scholar opened the books of the three insurers that run Medicare Advantage in Puerto Rico, MMM, Triple-S and MCS, from 2011 to 2022, and concluded that the island's plans are a profitable oligopoly living on public money while asking for more. This episode reads the same ledger and asks who wrote the first draft. The funding gap is real: benchmark payments about 38% below the states, about 26% after risk scores and quality bonuses. But the plans pay the island's physicians about 40% less than the states pay theirs, 99% of Puerto Rico's beneficiaries are in plans CMS rates 4.5 stars or better, and the plans clear the 85-cent medical loss ratio floor the Affordable Care Act wrote into law. The profit spikes the study flags, a 3.32% margin in 2020 with the medical loss ratio at a period low of 80.1%, are what capitation does when a hurricane or a pandemic empties the clinics while the per-member checks keep coming; in 2022, with utilization back and national owners in charge, the margin fell to negative 0.19%. The receipts: fence any new federal money with a 90% MLR floor, make vertical integration transparent, and give seniors a traditional Medicare option worth choosing. Underpaid, overstudied, and still the villain, by people who have never adjudicated a claim.
